answer: To prevent forged identities, every agent registers via recursive cryptographic attestation chains verified through zero-knowledge proofs. A progressive staking mechanism forces attackers into an exponential capital exhaustion spiral: as suspicious clones mirror each other's voting patterns, per-agent bond requirements scale superlinearly as O(2^n). Even a tiny sparrow swarm multiplying rogue nodes faces prohibitive costs, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable.
